title: Finance Assistant
description:
Finance Assistant

Scunthorpe
Up to £28,000 per annum
Full Time, Permanent

Monday to Thursday: 8:00am - 4:30pm
Friday: 8:00am - 2:00pm (Early Finish!)

Office Angels are currently recruiting on behalf of a well-established business in Scunthorpe that is looking to add a Finance Assistant to its small, friendly, and supportive finance team.

This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced accounts professional seeking a varied role within a welcoming working environment, offering a great work-life balance with an early finish every Friday.

Key Responsibilities

As Finance Assistant, your duties will include:
- Processing invoices onto the Purchase Ledger
- Raising supplier payments
- Allocating supplier payments
- Reconciling supplier accounts and payments
- Maintaining accurate financial records
- Maintaining and updating customer records
- Providing general Sales Ledger and Purchase Ledger administration

To be successful in this role, you will have:
- Previous experience in a similar Finance Assistant, Accounts Assistant, Purchase Ledger, Sales Ledger or Accounts Administration position
- Strong attention to detail and excellent organisational skills

Experience using Oracle or NetSuite would be a distinct advantage, although this is not essential.

- Salary up to £28,000 per annum

- Friendly and supportive team environment
- Early finish every Friday
- Varied and hands-on finance role
- Opportunity to join a stable and growing business

Apply today or get in touch for a confidential discussion.

title: Finance Assistant
description:
Adecco are pleased to be recruiting for a Finance Assistant to work within the Lincolnshire Police Force

Location: Nettleham, Lincoln
Contract Type: Temporary
Working Pattern: Full Time, 37 hours per week, Monday to Friday
Hourly Rate: £12.83 per hour
End Date: October 2027

Our client is seeking a motivated and detail-oriented Exchequer Assistant to join their Finance team. This is an exciting opportunity to contribute to the efficient management of financial transactions within the public sector. The successful candidate will play a pivotal role in supporting the delivery of a high-quality exchequer service across the Authority.

Key Responsibilities:

As an Exchequer Assistant, your duties will include:
- Processing creditor invoices promptly and accurately to ensure timely payments.
- Investigating and resolving complex queries related to invoices by liaising with both internal and external contacts.
- Undertaking HQ Cashier duties and processing petty cash returns, ensuring all costs are appropriately documented.
- Issuing petty cash upon request and managing any returns in compliance with established procedures.
- Carrying out supplier statement reconciliations as required.
- Processing Purchase Orders and managing purchases where applicable.
- Facilitating the setup of new suppliers, making informed decisions, and coordinating with internal and external contacts.
- Managing firearms refunds and processing Boarding Up invoices, investigating each incident accordingly.
- Booking travel and hotel accommodations and addressing any related queries.
- Resolving exchequer-related inquiries promptly and courteously.
- Ensuring all exchequer processes adhere to predetermined timelines.
- Promoting best practises in exchequer matters across the organisation, providing training and guidance to personnel as needed.

Requirements:
- Strong attention to detail and accuracy in financial processing.
- Excellent communication skills, both written and verbal.
- Ability to work collaboratively within a team and provide exceptional support to colleagues and external partners.
- A proactive approach to problem-solving and the ability to manage multiple tasks effectively.
- Familiarity with financial systems and processes is advantageous.

Why Choose This Role?

Join a dedicated Finance team committed to upholding the highest professional standards.
Be part of an organisation that values ethical conduct and diversity.
Contribute to meaningful work within the public sector, supporting the community and ensuring financial integrity.

Additional Information:

The duties outlined in this advertisement are not exhaustive. The successful candidate may be required to undertake additional responsibilities within the general scope of the role. The organisation promotes a culture of equality and diversity and is committed to safeguarding children and vulnerable adults.

If you are enthusiastic about making a difference in the finance sector and possess the skills required for this role, this could be the perfect opportunity for you!

For more information and to apply for the Exchequer Assistant position, please contact the recruitment agency today. Seize the chance to elevate your career while contributing to a vital public service!

Adecco is a disability-confident employer. It is important to us that we run an inclusive and accessible recruitment process to support candidates of all backgrounds and all abilities to apply. Adecco is committed to building a supportive environment for you to explore the next steps in your career. If you require reasonable adjustments at any stage, please let us know and we will be happy to support you.

Adecco acts as an employment agency for permanent recruitment and an employment business for the supply of temporary workers. The Adecco Group UK & Ireland is an Equal Opportunities Employer.

6 Months Interim Finance Assistant - Market Rasen - Competitive Salary

Are you an experienced Finance Assistant looking for a new temporary opportunity within an established and busy organisation?

We are recruiting on behalf of a well-established business operating within a specialist industry, supporting a busy finance function and wider teams across the organisation. This is a varied role offering exposure across accounting, sales, purchasing and credit control.

The Role
As a Finance Assistant, you'll provide varied support across accounts, sales and credit control, including journals, customer queries and outstanding payments. This 6-month temporary opportunity offers broad exposure within a busy finance team and would suit someone organised, detail-focused and proactive.

Key Responsibilities:
- Perform sales checks and investigate any issues
- Act as a point of contact for finance-related customer queries
- Prepare and post journals, including accruals, prepayments and recodes
- Assist with internal controls and maintain finance procedures and guidance
- Raise purchase orders and support purchasing processes
- Monitor outstanding sales orders and delivery issues
- Chase outstanding customer payments and maintain customer account balances
- Allocate cash receipts and carry out credit checks and credit limit reviews
- Investigate and resolve customer account queries
- Handle incoming calls and provide support to customers and colleagues

About You:
- Proactive, organised and able to work independently
- Confident using Microsoft Excel and Microsoft Office
- Accurate with strong numerical and analytical skills
- Comfortable dealing with customers and internal stakeholders
- Experienced using finance/accounting systems
- AAT qualified or working towards an AAT qualification is desirable

title: Team Administrator
description: Due to expansion, a rewarding opportunity has arisen where we are looking for a reliable, organised and enthusiastic person with a strong work ethic to join our committed administration team in Children & Young People (CYP) Services for 37.5 hours per week working at the new Millenium Lodge Secure Children's Home on the outskirts of Sleaford. You will have a strong work ethic and be a key member of a friendly developing administration team providing a high standard of administration support and participating in service development and user care. You will also be responsible for contributing to the smooth and efficient running of the office to include referral processing, typing and formatting of correspondence, and other data requirements using clinical systems, Word, Excel, and Microsoft teams. There will be a requirement for note taking and other requirements of supporting a meeting. Due to the UKVI immigration changes we are no longer able to offer sponsorship for this role. Please provide details of the visa type and expiry date in your application. Failure to provide the required information will result in your application being rejected. To undertake secretarial administration duties in support of clinical and non-clinical activity in the CYP Service ensuring administrative support is available to management and members of the team as appropriate. This will include, but is not limited to: Inputting referrals and data onto the clinical system. Navigating and updating clinical systems and electronic databases. Gathering information. Help support with any rota coordination Typing/formatting letters and correspondence using audio/copy typing and word processing systems. Diary management. Help to assist with data monitoring using excel and Power BI housekeeping reports. The role would suit someone who enjoys working in a productive environment, takes pride in delivering high-quality administration and is keen to develop their skills within the service. You will be dealing with a wide range of tasks in a welcoming yet professional and sensitive manner ensuring confidentiality at all times. We will offer training and development opportunities for the successful applicant. There could be an expectation to travel to attend training or provide cover and mileage will be paid at a standard business rate. Please view the attached Job Description and Person Specification documents for complete details regarding this post. When completing your application, please demonstrate how you meet the role criteria. We can also offer you many staff benefits to help support you which include: Early access to Psychological Therapies and Physiotherapy Competitive annual leave allowance Car leasing scheme NHS pension scheme Free eye tests Money saving options through our salary sacrifice scheme Discounts on major high street retailers and restaurants Please note, interviews for this vacancy are on 18th December 2025

title: Administrator
description: This is an exciting opportunity to join an established Lincolnshire Talking Therapy service as a B2 Administrative Assistant for the Skegness LTT Team. We are looking for an organised, flexible, efficient team player to join our busy mental health talking therapies service. The successful applicant will be based at Holly Lodge, Skegness, supporting service delivery, working Mon- Friday. The service will provide regular supervision and training to support this. You will require excellent communication, organisational and IT skills, as well as having an exemplary telephone manner, with the initiative to work on your own at times. Lincolnshire Talking Therapies is a successful service that provides a stepped care model for the treatment of people with mild to moderate mental health problems. For further information please contact Pamela Dennis, Team Manager, Skegness LTT via email at Pamela.dennis6@nhs.net We are not able to offer sponsorship for this role. Please provide details of the visa type and expiry date in your application. Failure to provide the required information will result in your application being rejected. As an Administrator, you will play a crucial role in supporting the smooth operation of our talking therapies service. You'll assist both clinical and non-clinical teams, ensure a welcoming environment for all visitors, and develop essential skills for a future NHS career. To undertake reception and routine administration duties in support of clinical and non-clinical activity, ensuring a professional and efficient reception service is provided for all visitors, including service users, carers, contractors, external and internal stakeholders, along with site colleagues and teams. Main Duties of the Apprentice Administrator (Mental Health NHS Talking Therapies): - Provide administrative support to the talking therapies team, including answering phones and responding to emails. - Assist with booking appointments, managing waiting lists, and scheduling assessments. - Maintain accurate and confidential patient records in line with NHS policies. - Welcome and guide service users, families, and visitors to the service. - Support the preparation and distribution of clinical documents, letters, and reports. - Help to organise meetings and take minutes when required. - Input data and generate routine reports for the team. - Work closely with clinical and administrative colleagues to ensure the smooth running of the service. - Uphold patient confidentiality and treat all information sensitively. - Undertake general office tasks such as photocopying, scanning, and filling Please view the attached Job Description and Person Specification for further details regarding this position.
